clue.text: Half-heartedly swears on late pardons

indicators.note: in a down-or-across charade, 'on' places the swearing word after the word for late

parts.note: ex- means former, so late (as in 'the late chairman') gives EX

indicators.note: half of the heart, the doubled middle letters, is taken away from the swearing word

parts.note: to swear is to cuss, giving CUSSES

explanation.surface: Someone cursing over being late while offering apologies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' means losing half the heart: one of the two central letters goes. 'Late' is the former sense, as in 'ex-'.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone is to forgive or let them off, a straight synonym of the verb pardon.

clue.text: Tribe of Israel record that man accepting Egyptian god

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the pronoun takes in the god

parts.note: him refers to that man
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A tribe keeps a record of a man who embraced an Egyptian deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephraim, son of Joseph, was founder of one of the twelve tribes of Israel.

clue.text: Island goat refusing grain

indicators.note: refusing means turning down, so the grain is cut out

parts.note: Capricorn is the goat sign of the zodiac
corn is grain

explanation.surface: An island goat that won't eat its corn.
explanation.definitionFit: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples.

clue.text: Heavens, half of spirit's gone

indicators.note: half of the word, with the 's gone' marking that the other half is lost, leaves its last half

parts.note: whisky is a spirit

explanation.surface: A cry of 'Heavens!' on finding half the whisky gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of spirit's gone' means the first half, WHI, has disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The sky is the heavens, the vault above the earth.

clue.text: Spooner's secret vessel that contains disinfectant for Cambridge, say

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two synonyms trade starts

parts.note: deep can mean secret or hidden, as in a deep plot
a ship is a vessel

explanation.surface: A secret vessel holding a cleaning fluid for a university city.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge here is a breed of sheep, not the university town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep dip is the insecticidal wash farmers use on sheep; the Cambridge is a sheep breed.

clue.text: Rules of golf concerning playing partners?

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
over can mean about or concerning, as in 'a row over money'
in bridge North and South play as partners, abbreviated NS; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A question about the rules of golf for people who play together.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S are the compass seats at the bridge table; North-South form one partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler governs a country, so 'rules' as a verb is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Swelling old vice-president secures appeal

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so the politician holds the appeal word

parts.note: Al Gore was US vice-president under Clinton
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A former vice-president with a swollen neck making an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A goitre is an enlargement of the thyroid gland, a swelling in the neck.

clue.text: Temptress and siren, when exposed, wound up bloody parasites

parts.note: a vamp is a seductive woman, a temptress

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of covering, so the outer letters go
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to stab is to wound

explanation.surface: A seductive woman and a siren, once unmasked, turn out to be bloodsuckers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips SIREN to IRE; 'up' reverses STAB. 'Wound up' looks like an adjective meaning tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Vampire bats are bats that feed on the blood of other animals, so literally bloody parasites.

clue.text: Dexter is on this fit team

parts.note: right can mean healthy or fit, as in 'right as rain'
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Someone named Dexter plays for this healthy team.
explanation.walkthrough: Dexter is Latin for right; in heraldry the dexter side is the right, so dexter lies on it.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry dexter denotes the shield's right-hand half, so it belongs on that side.

clue.text: Rustled up pastry

indicators.note: rustled up suggests something thrown together, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Making a quick pastry from what is to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a pastry of thin layered dough rolled round a filling such as apple.

clue.text: Environment settling on fortunate compromise

indicators.note: in this across clue, the word for environment comes to rest after the word for fortunate

parts.note: happy can mean lucky or fortunate, as in a happy accident
a medium is the surroundings an organism lives in, an environment

explanation.surface: An environment settling on a lucky outcome sounds like a negotiation ending.
explanation.definitionFit: A happy medium is an idiom for a satisfactory middle way between two extremes.

clue.text: Wrangle about fish

indicators.note: about signals turning the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: to rag someone is to tease or argue with them, a wrangle

explanation.surface: Arguing over a fish, perhaps at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: The gar is a long-snouted fish, sometimes called garfish or needlefish.

clue.text: Peg out wearing gold for so long

indicators.note: the gold symbol wears the dying word as clothing, wrapped round it

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to peg out is slang for to die

explanation.surface: Someone dying in their gold finery bids farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French farewell used in English, as is the informal goodbye 'so long'.

clue.text: Awful bus lane disrupted around maximum traffic?

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters go round the other word
disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: peak is the time of heaviest traffic, as in peak hour; the question mark flags the loose sense

explanation.surface: A bus lane disrupted at rush hour makes for an awful journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges BUS LANE into UNS-ABLE, with PEAK going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unspeakable means too bad to be expressed in words, so dreadful or awful.

clue.text: Failing edit, press gets stuck

indicators.note: something failing has broken down, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A printing press jams while an edit goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stuck at something is to have persevered or kept going, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Water supply trouble in biggest course?

parts.note: the mains are the public supply pipes for water
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A problem with the water supply in the most important course of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' is a sailing term for the lowest sail on a square-rigged mast; the biggest is the main one. The surface pushes toward a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: In sailing the courses are the lowest sails, and the largest of them on the mainmast is this sail.

clue.text: During passage, nothing lost from recycling change of key

indicators.note: recycling sends letters round from one end to the other
lost from means the zero letter is dropped out of the music word

parts.note: a transition in music is a change of key, a modulation
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A musician moving between keys, losing nothing along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: TRANSITION less O is TRANSITIN; 'recycling' moves IN from the end to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: In transit means while on the way somewhere, so during a passage or journey.

clue.text: Lofty, aggressive, gutless Den's back

indicators.note: with no guts, only the outside letters of the word remain
back signals the den word read in reverse

parts.note: a den is a lair, an animal's home

explanation.surface: A cowardly aggressor called Den returns, held to be high-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutless' leaves AE from 'aggressive'; 'back' turns LAIR into RIAL. Den is a lair, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerial means existing high in the air, so lofty in the literal sense of elevated.

clue.text: Brandy from Moldova regularly picked up?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the letters chosen sound like the answer

parts.note: taking the letters of Moldova at regular intervals, every second one, gives O, D and V, said aloud as three letter names

explanation.surface: Brandy imported from Moldova on a regular basis.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'Moldova' are O, D, V; said as letters they sound like 'eau de vie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie, French for water of life, is a clear fruit brandy.

clue.text: Run into position, quietly giving update

indicators.note: into tells us the run letter goes inside the position word

parts.note: a site is a position or location
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: Instructions to rush into place without a noise and report back.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitrep is military shorthand for a situation report, a brief status update.

clue.text: What remains after shaping deal

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber, and shaping it with a saw leaves fine wood particles behind

explanation.surface: What is left over once an agreement is shaped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' looks like an agreement, but it is softwood timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawing wood leaves a residue of fine particles, which is what sawing deal leaves.

clue.text: A comb pinched by indulged bird

indicators.note: pinched means held tight, so the pampering word holds the other letters

parts.note: to pet is to pamper or indulge
to rake is to comb through, as with a rake over soil

explanation.surface: A spoilt pet steals a comb.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small, long-tailed parrot, so a bird by example.

clue.text: Distress people in wrong

indicators.note: in places the people word within the wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are people

explanation.surface: People in the wrong cause suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is great suffering or anguish, so distress as a noun.

clue.text: Comic menace erred when doing a U-turn

indicators.note: doing a U-turn means going back the way it came, reversing the letters

parts.note: to sin is to err, giving sinned

explanation.surface: A troublemaker who did wrong and then changed course.
explanation.definitionFit: Dennis the Menace is a mischievous boy in the British children's comic The Beano.

clue.text: Feeble dope, holding three high cards, extremely naive

indicators.note: the drug word holds the cards and the other letters inside it

parts.note: weed is slang for cannabis, dope
A and K abbreviate ace and king, here an ace and two kings

indicators.note: extremely takes only the outer letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A weak, drug-using card player holding a strong hand and looking very green.
explanation.walkthrough: The three high cards are an ace and two kings; 'extremely' gives the ends of 'naive', and 'holding' splits the drug word after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak-kneed describes someone lacking resolve or courage, the sense of feeble here.

clue.text: I slipped around entrance to race track

indicators.note: around tells us the exclamation is turned to read backwards

parts.note: Oops! is what someone says on slipping or blundering

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling at the gate of a racetrack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I slipped' stands for the exclamation a person makes on slipping, and 'around' reverses it. 'Race track' wants to be one phrase; 'track' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of an animal, its footprints or droppings, so a track being followed.

clue.text: Jaguar darted when uncaged

indicators.note: uncaged means let out of its outer bars, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: pounced means sprang suddenly, darted

explanation.surface: A big cat dashing out once released from its cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaguar' could be the car, but it is the cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ounce is a name for the snow leopard and has also been applied to other wild cats such as the jaguar.

clue.text: Notes evenly spaced — quite so

indicators.note: evenly spaced picks the even-numbered letters, at regular intervals

explanation.surface: Musical notes placed at even intervals, agreed to with 'quite so'.
explanation.walkthrough: Ut is the old name for the note now called do, in the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In early sol-fa singing the first degree of the scale was named ut; the plural gives several such notes.

clue.text: Social worker, inviting new outrage, one lacking in generosity

indicators.note: inviting means taking in a guest, so the bee word takes in the letter for new

parts.note: a bee is a worker in a social insect colony

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the numeral is dropped

parts.note: violence is an outrage or atrocity
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A social worker welcomes a fresh scandal while one person lacks generosity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a profession, but means a bee. BENE plus VOLENCE (violence missing I).
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolence is kindness and a disposition to do good, so open-handed generosity.

clue.text: Porky Pig naked in 'Looney Tune' with censored content

indicators.note: in places the middle letter inside the outer pair
censored content means the inside is cut, leaving only the outer letters
naked means stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: The cartoon pig appears without clothes in a cut cartoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky' is rhyming slang: porky pie, a lie. The cartoon character Porky Pig is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Porky, short for porky pie in Cockney rhyming slang, is British slang for a falsehood.

clue.text: Broken trust restricting French art teacher once

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the shuffled letters close round the French word
a broken word is knocked into a new arrangement

parts.note: in French tu es means you are, so es is the old English art

explanation.surface: Broken trust keeping a French art teacher from the past in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges TRUST to TUTRS, which holds ES. 'Art' is the archaic 'thou art', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutress is an old word for a female tutor, so a teacher, and 'once' flags it as dated.

clue.text: Head away from most dangerous mountain

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which goes away

parts.note: severest means harshest or most dangerous

explanation.surface: Advice to turn away from the deadliest peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest mountain, an example of the class.
